observations.trace: The full historical slot source equals the 95e body. Core InputAddressMapping supplies static input labels and typed locations; keyboard_slots converts each label to a native key, cycles among eligible locations and retains the input label plus location index. HUD JSON SlotHudPress admits a String, finds an exact static mapping and ignores an unknown value before calling the same slot selection. An empty mapping has an empty find_map range, so the modulo expression is not reached.
observations.remaining: The earlier c100 candidate NEW-HUD-SLOT-INPUT-001 is re-assessed at 95e using exact byte identity of all eleven prior scoped sources and bounded fresh reads. It remains an identity/ownership question, not a proven key mismatch; broader consumer and alias coverage remains open. Earlier tests were source only.

observations.trace: Parsed TacticalAudioConfig checks positive finite base rustle pitch and independently positive ordered finite pitch endpoints, but not their product. As already assessed at c100, finite factors around 1e30 multiply beyond finite f32, while factors around 1e-30 produce a value below the smallest positive f32 subnormal. The 95e PlaybackSpeed wrapper retains and multiplies the raw factors, the wasm backend passes the speed to sfxPlay, and a loaded positive-length worklet voice with zero speed remains at position zero until replaced.
observations.remaining: This is the same earlier 059 pitch contract and c100 browser-boundary consequence, not an additional unique finding. The YAML parser, extreme custom configuration, contact/rustle, loaded sound and active browser are conditional; shipped ordinary tuning is not alleged bad. No parser, arithmetic probe, sound or runtime ran.

observations.trace: ActiveTacticalScene explicitly chooses the most recently activated live SceneEnvironment and falls back through live predecessors on removal; apply_active_environment_fog consumes that entity. Rain audio independently takes the first environment, first listener and first ground and does not tie them to that selected scene. If two scenes differ and query order selects another row, the audio inputs need not correspond to the canonical scene.
observations.remaining: This is the existing 059 rain scene finding, not a new unique issue. Actual overlap duration, ground/listener ownership, sound asset readiness, audibility and full aliases remain unverified. Wind also takes first environment, a related source question, but is not assumed an exact alias.

observations.trace: Earlier e275 P01-L11-CURRENT-UNPLAYABLE-AUDIO-REQUEST-LIFETIME concerned Bevy AudioPlayer entities whose requested Despawn required playback to begin. At 95e the inspected movement and combat one-shots call sound_output::play_spatial instead; the non-wasm backend is explicitly silent and browser sfxPlay drops one-shots while its mixer is unavailable, its asset is unready, or the frame start cap is reached.
observations.remaining: The old retained-entity mechanism stays attached to e275, with no inference of runtime growth or a whole-application negative proof at 95e. The current failed-load cache question is separate; intentional unlock and bounded voice policies remain distinct.

observations.trace: The strategic backdrop spawns its environment under the retained scene root. Browser EnterTactical queues release_scene before establishing a tactical client; release_scene despawns the root. If no other environment is available and update_wind_volume then runs, its early return sends no new wind gain. In the inspected JavaScript backend the previous loop gain remains in its loop slot until a later sfxLoop update. Pinned Bevy ECS hierarchy source describes child despawn with the parent.
observations.remaining: This needs an already loaded, playing nonzero wind loop, a frame without any environment and an active browser mixer. Whether continuity or silence is desired during scene handoff is a product policy question; no actual transition, audible effect or all-writer/global lifetime conclusion is claimed.

observations.trace: sfx.js inserts {id, ready:false} into its sounds map before fetching and decoding. Its rejection handler logs a warning but does not remove or mark the entry for retry; later load(path) returns the existing unready object. sfxPlay drops requests for an unready object, and an existing loop.sound remains that same object, so a transient failed fetch/decode can leave that sound unavailable for the lifetime of this script instance even after the external condition clears.
observations.remaining: No network failure, decoder error, playback or recovery was observed. A reload creates a new script instance; explicit retry/failure and user-facing policy are not established. Suspended-audio dropping and active-voice limits are documented intentional modes and are not this first failure.

dependencies: Establish desired silence or continuity during scene handoff and failure; determine all scene lifecycle and any other gain writers.
Trace whether an active loop and no-environment frame occur in supported entry/exit paths, with browser scheduling and native output separately qualified.
acceptance_requirements: The no-scene state has an explicit, reviewable gain policy and follows that policy through scene removal and replacement.
Preserve intended smooth rain and looping continuity where applicable.
